question: You are extending the Appian KB sync so a user can view an object's code as it was at an earlier release. Where does the code come from at read time, what must the KB itself never store, and how does a past release resolve?
answer_points: Code is fetched live from the connected environment through the Appian Dev MCP, version-parameterized (get_object_code with an optional version) — never from the KB.
The KB stores only metadata, structure, the dependency graph and recomputed bundles; it must never persist SAIL source (ADR-037).
A past release resolves through kb_releases (a named pointer: sync_id + env_version_ref) over the temporal SCD-2 history (valid_from_sync / valid_to_sync).
